title: hawkes-engine: multivariate Hawkes processes with trust calibration
description:
Multivariate Hawkes processes with exponential kernels for Python: a compiled likelihood and gradient, a maximum-likelihood fit with standard errors, two independent exact simulators, time-rescaling diagnostics, and a lookup of what a pre-registered simulation study measured about the fit's standard errors in a given regime.

The calibration map comes from a pre-registered study of 128 simulation cells with 2000 replications each, frozen before the data existed at the tag H6-preregistration with six dated amendments. Its principal finding is a limitation: pooled over the two-type cells with at least 2000 events, the standard errors the fit reports are 0.779 (95% interval 0.757 to 0.801) times the empirical standard deviation of its estimates. That pooled figure is dominated by the tail of the estimate distribution rather than by the width of the interval: at the anchor cell the decay block's ratio is 0.007 on the mean statistic and 0.835 on its median-based companion, computed from the same replications. Two of the six pre-registered hypotheses were not confirmed, and the estimator is undefined where the observation window holds only a fraction of one decay time. The library reports what was measured and where nothing was.

From 0.3.0 a second pre-registered study, frozen at the tag SW-preregistration, tests whether a sandwich covariance estimator closes that gap. It does not. The information equality holds to within the finite-window effect, with the ratio of score covariance to information between 0.951 and 1.053 coordinate by coordinate, so a sandwich differs from the inverse Hessian by at most a factor of 1.026 and cannot account for a shortfall of the size measured. The null is reported as a null, and it locates the shortfall outside the term the work had previously named.

Every figure quoted here is emitted from a committed output rather than typed, and published pages are pinned to their sources by a test suite that fails when the two disagree.
notes: 0.1.0 was deposited manually; the first automatic deposit for a later release may need to be queued in the Zenodo web UI. The preregistration is at the annotated tag H6-preregistration.
